Planet X and SPHEREx · November 14, 2026

How can you tell if the sky changed?

Open two genuine SPHEREx dates and check their wavelengths, masks and registration before interpreting a shift. Save a question with its sky coordinates and export the source records with your investigation.

Open two DR1 dates → Try matched-wavelength playback → Search your own coordinates →

The five challenge fields

These bounded QR2/D2 field tests use cached sky cutouts. Each link opens measured pixels with its observation dates and source records. The tests establish which frames were usable in these requests. Scientific review is pending.

Barnard’s Star
1 frame. A single frame cannot show motion. The preset uses a J2000 search centre for this high proper-motion star.
Epsilon Indi B
2 frames. The data prepared here do not resolve the Ba/Bb components or establish motion.
WISE 0855
2 frames. The test uses the challenge coordinates. Identifying a moving source needs independent checks.
RW Aurigae
3 frames. Masked support and wavelength comparisons limit interpretation of apparent brightness changes.
R Draconis
2 frames in the original bounded test. Open the focused two-date assessment for individual measurements and rejection evidence. Calibrated variability remains unestablished.

Data sources and credits

  • SPHEREx images, masks, timestamps and calibration records come from NASA/IPAC IRSA. The official notebooks explain cutouts and FITS extensions. Mission archive ↗ · Tutorial notebooks ↗ · DR1 spectral images DOI ↗ · QR3 DOI ↗ · QR2 DOI ↗ · IRSA usage terms ↗
  • Gaia DR3 provides astrometric references for the screened historical comparison and the matched-wavelength example. Gaia at MAST ↗ · Gaia DR3 citation ↗
  • WiseView’s flipbook is the interaction precedent for stepping through infrared observations. WiseView ↗
  • NEOSSat is an independent near-Earth observing mission. These partner resources provide background and a separate path to its observations. CSA mission ↗ · Canadian Astronomy Data Centre ↗ · CSA tutorial ↗ · NEOSSat dataset ↗

This publication makes use of data products from the Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization and Ices Explorer (SPHEREx), which is a joint project of the Jet Propulsion Laboratory and the California Institute of Technology, and is funded by the National Aeronautics and Space Administration.

This work has made use of data from the European Space Agency (ESA) mission Gaia, processed by the Gaia Data Processing and Analysis Consortium (DPAC). SKYSHIFT is an independent Project Mercury Team application. Methods, provenance and additional credits →

Sources, methods & SKYSHIFT

Challenge fields & data sources → Play spacecraft introduction →

SKYSHIFT is an independent Project Mercury Team application. It uses real SPHEREx observations with original source identities, calibration records and conservative quality masks.

The restricted M101 comparison has passed documented engineering screens. Internal human review and qualified scientific approval remain PENDING. Questions are user hypotheses, not detections or confirmed changes.
